newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa dives as disappointed longs raid marke.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa dives as disappointed longs raid marke.

text.p: Sellers raided London's cocoa futures on Monday afternoon, slashing benchmark prices by nearly five percent as prospects for a rally vanished.
Aggressive sellers offered the key May contract down to 879 stg a tonne, letting it slip through the previous contract low of 885 stg in a hunt for support.
"I think it's liquidation of longs disappointed by the lack of follow through and a bit of a bear raid," said one trader.
Turnover on the exchange reached a hefty 11,837 lots which whipped up bearish sentiment as the market reeled from an attempt last week to jolt out of a prolonged downtrend.
But traders noted large volumes of crosses and switches including the distant March, May and September contracts.
Wednesday's 45-stg slump in May comes after a technical sell-off in New York on Tuesday and a stronger sterling against European crosses which makes London vulnerable to selling.
Sell stops were triggered as May stumbled at 920, a key support, and the psychological 900 mark.
"On Friday we went home thinking the market has turned the corner, but in no way we believed sterling was going to be so strong," said one trader.
"Now I don't think anybody would like to go home now with a long position," he added.
Cargill, who sold aggressively earlier this week, almost instigating the rout, continued to sell, attracting other long holders to close their positions and others to go short.
Origins were also active close to the market, tempted by sterling's fresh gains against the French franc which is the currency some African producers deal in.
Tuesday's sharp losses kindled speculation that one major trade house were winding down their longs after the market's declining prospects for a continued upside run.
Stronger-then-expected arrival numbers in Ivory Coast and Ghana also depressed sentiment this week, traders said.
Technically, March is expected to find support at 850, but lower levels might carry the second-month May down to 850, traders said.
March/May traded at nearly 30 stg at one stage before the close, compared with 22-23 earlier in the day. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom 44-171-542 8072
